personnel. Filed under /Firm/Standards/.

Appendix A - Firm Reference Values (Sections 3.4 and 6)
The firm concrete table, firm assembly library, and firm reference table for the fuel and flame temperature range cited
in Sections 3.4 and 6 are reproduced below. Solid-region properties are held constant over the design range absent
case-specific data.
- Printed siliceous-aggregate concrete (outer/inner leaf): k = 1.4 W/(m*K), rho = 2200 kg/m3, cp = 900 J/(kg*K).
- Galvanized steel ties: k = 45 W/(m*K), rho = 7850 kg/m3, cp = 490 J/(kg*K).

Cavity emissivities (Section 6), grey diffuse:

[Normal] 1. Purpose
[Normal] This DRAFT is the interim client summary of the ASCE 7-22 structural wind-load extraction called out under SOW Section 3.2, and covers the pressure rollup produced from the wall-probe extraction run on 10/09/2025. The scope is limited to the standalone structural wind-load case; the Section 3.1 wildfire matrix is handled separately and is not addressed here.
[Normal] Section 3.2 asks the firm to develop the code-basis wall pressures at the OAS-WUI-01 envelope for a discrete-wind-speed check independent of the wildfire matrix, and to report peak pressures on windward, side, and leeward faces at probe locations laid out in the case verification plan. The values summarized below are drawn directly from the interim probe extraction (interim_wall_pressures.csv, 10/09/2025) with no post-processing beyond the peak rollup.
[Normal] 2. Case Description
[List Bullet] Basis of loading: ASCE 7-22 (Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures).
[List Bullet] Site: Tucson, Arizona (Ocotillo pilot envelope, OAS-WUI-01_revC geometry of record).
[List Bullet] Basic wind speed, V: 96 mph (Risk Category II mapped value for the Tucson site).
[List Bullet] Exposure category: C (open terrain with scattered obstructions, consistent with the Avra Valley WUI setting).
[List Bullet] Risk category: II.
[List Bullet] Mean roof height, h: 6.4 m.
[List Bullet] Directionality and topography factors and the velocity-pressure exposure coefficient are applied per ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26 at the mean roof height; wall pressure coefficients on windward, side, and leeward faces are taken from Chapter 27 (directional procedure, enclosed low-rise building) at the site aspect ratio.
[Normal] The probe grid used for peak extraction consists of ten windward probes spanning the windward face, five probes on each side wall (north and south), and five probes on the leeward face. Probe elevations are 0.8 m, 3.2 m, and 5.6 m above grade. All probe values reported are peak (envelope) values from the interim extraction.
[Normal] 3. Results
[Normal] The table below reproduces the peak pressures from the interim extraction file exactly as recorded.
<<TABLE>>
Wall surface | Peak pressure | Governing probe
Windward wall | 12.4 Pa | WW_02, WW_03, WW_04, WW_06, WW_07, WW_08
Side wall (peak suction) | −9.5 Pa | SW_S_01
Leeward wall (peak suction) | −6.1 Pa | LW_01, LW_03
<<END>>
[Normal] Sign convention: positive pressures act inward on the wall face; negative pressures indicate suction (outward). Values are peaks across the interim probe set; the full per-probe listing is retained in interim_wall_pressures.csv.
[Normal] 4. Discussion
[Normal] Taken at face value, the pressures returned by the interim rollup are negligible relative to the structural design demand envelope typically associated with the framing of a 6.4 m mean-roof-height enclosed building at a 96 mph basic wind speed in Exposure C. A 12.4 Pa peak windward pressure is a very small fraction of the wall loads that would ordinarily drive sizing of tie, header, and out-of-plane bending checks for a printed-concrete assembly of this scale, and the corresponding side-wall and leeward suctions (−9.5 Pa and −6.1 Pa peak) are similarly small.
[Normal] On that basis the interim reading is that the ASCE 7-22 wall loading, taken as extracted, does not govern the OAS-WUI-01 envelope. Wildfire-driven radiative and convective loading (SOW Section 3.1) and the E119 fire-endurance envelope remain the controlling design considerations for the assembly. No structural remediation of the OAS-WUI-01_revC envelope is indicated by this interim result.
[Normal] The client should treat these figures as provisional pending peer review under the firm's QA workflow. ========= CFDME-2025-041_scoping_memo_20251008.docx
[Normal] THE CFD ME   |   Tucson, Arizona   |   AZ PE #48213   |   CFDME-2025-041 rev A
[Normal] MEMORANDUM — PHASE 1 SCOPING
<<TABLE>>
To: | Project file — CFDME-2025-041 Ocotillo WUI, Phase 1
From: | Gordon Selby, PE — Owner & Principal Engineer, The CFD ME
Reviewed by: | Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer
Date: | 10/08/2025
Subject: | Phase 1 scoping — first-principles fire-source, regime-assessment, and sub-domain basis for the wildfire LES set
<<END>>
[Normal] 1.  Purpose & Scope
[Normal] This memo fixes, at project kickoff and before any meshing is undertaken, the first-principles basis on which the Phase 1 wildfire-exposure large-eddy simulation set will be built. It records the design conditions taken from the site meteorological pull, the buffelgrass fuel model, the Rothermel-to-Byram source-term chain that produces the design fire, the Froude regime assessment inputs, and the LES sub-domain geometry against which downstream mesh sizing will be measured. It is issued on the effective date of the Ocotillo Additive Structures Phase 1 Statement of Work (CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01, signed 10/08/2025), before revC of the assembly geometry (OAS-WUI-01_revC, transmitted with the SOW) is imported into the mesher.
[Normal] The intent is that every downstream case-setup artifact, mesh-study artifact, and Phase 1 reporting deliverable — including the interim hand-calc due 10/13/2025 and the LES setup deliverable due 10/20/2025 — trace their source-term, regime, and geometry inputs back to the numbers recorded here, rather than re-argue them case-by-case. Where a downstream artifact needs the design fire heat release, the characteristic source diameter, or the plume length scale, it shall cite this memo.
[Normal] The scope of Phase 1 as procured under Section 3.1 of the SOW is six transient wildfire cases (240 deg and 270 deg wind directions at 20-ft wind speeds of 5, 8, and 12 m/s). The fire source term and the sub-domain sizing recorded here apply to that entire matrix; they are not per-case parameters.
[Normal] 2.  Site Design Conditions
[Normal] Design conditions are taken from the ten-year hourly record of the Pima County ALERT network for the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson (data pull: site_met_avra_valley_2015-2024.csv, Section 3.1 of the SOW envelope). The following envelope governs Phase 1:
<<TABLE>>
Quantity | Design value | Basis
Ambient temperature | 35–42 °C | 95th-percentile daytime summer envelope, ALERT record
Relative humidity | 10–25 % | Coincident with the temperature envelope, same record
Wind speed at 20 ft | 5–12 m/s | Matrix speeds 5, 8, 12 m/s per SOW §3.1
Site | Sonoran Desert buffelgrass WUI, Avra Valley west of Tucson | SOW §2 “Site”
<<END>>
[Normal] These conditions define the site for regime classification (Section 4 below) and for the source-term chain (Section 3 below). They are the same conditions carried into the Phase 1 report; no re-derivation is required.
[Normal] 3.  Fuel Model — Sonoran Buffelgrass at Site Design Conditions
[Normal] The design fire source term is developed under the Rothermel spread-to-Byram intensity chain, evaluated at the site design conditions of Section 2. The buffelgrass fuel model is adopted per the SOW Section 2 definition (“Buffelgrass Fuel Model”). Fuel-model quantities are:
[Normal] •  Fuel load (dry):  w = 0.6 kg/m²
[Normal] •  Low heat of combustion:  h = 18,600 kJ/kg
[Normal] •  Rate of spread at design wind:  R = 0.9 m/s
[Normal] R is the head-fire rate of spread produced by the Rothermel surface-fire spread model for cured buffelgrass at the low-humidity, high-temperature, moderate-wind conditions of Section 2. It is used here as the input to the Byram fireline-intensity relation; the Rothermel-model input parameter tabulation for buffelgrass is on file with the project data pull.
[Normal] Byram’s fireline intensity is the product of the low heat of combustion, the available fuel load per unit area, and the rate of spread:
[Normal] I = h · w · R
[Normal]   = (18,600 kJ/kg) × (0.6 kg/m²) × (0.9 m/s)
[Normal]   = 10,040 kW/m
[Normal] The Byram wind-tilted solid-flame length correlation gives:
[Normal] L = 0.0775 · I^0.46
[Normal]   = 0.0775 × (10,040)^0.46
[Normal]   = 5.4 m
[Normal] L above is the wind-tilted Byram flame length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height and is not comparable to Heskestad’s still-air correlation (see Section 5 for the idealization record).
[Normal] 4.  Froude / Regime Assessment
[Normal] Regime selection follows CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §2. The controlling non-dimensional group is the Froude number formed on the characteristic source diameter of the LES sub-domain:
[Normal] Fr = u_wind / sqrt(g · D_char)
[Normal] Taking D_char = 3.0 m (the LES sub-domain segment fixed in Section 5 below) and g = 9.81 m/s²:
[Normal] sqrt(g · D_char) = sqrt(9.81 × 3.0) = sqrt(29.43) = 5.42 m/s
[Normal] Evaluated across the site design wind envelope 5–12 m/s:
<<TABLE>>
u_wind | Fr = u_wind / sqrt(g · D_char)
5 m/s | 0.92
8 m/s | 1.48
12 m/s | 2.21
<<END>>
[Normal] The Froude / plume-velocity ratio falls in the range ~0.9–2.2 across the entire design envelope.
[Normal] Regime classification.  Classification against the Modeling Standard §2 thresholds, and solver selection per §3 of that standard, shall be carried out and documented in the case setup record before any case in this matrix is meshed.
[Normal] This classification is made once, at the firm level, for the entire Phase 1 wildfire matrix; it is not re-argued case-by-case within the envelope.
[Normal] 5.  LES Sub-Domain
[Normal] The LES sub-domain represents a 3.0 m segment of the flaming front. This segment length is the characteristic source width used for the plume model, and the value of D_char used in the Section 4 Froude computation and in the plume-length-scale computation below.
[Normal] 5.1  Line vs Axisymmetric Reconciliation
[Normal] The Byram fireline-intensity relation of Section 3 gives an intensity per unit length of the fire front (kW/m). The plume length scale D* referred to by the firm modeling and verification standards is an axisymmetric-source property (kW total). The two quantities are not interchangeable and cannot be composed directly. The 3.0 m segment length is the specific conversion factor between them for this project: it defines how much fire-front length is captured within one LES sub-domain, and therefore what total heat release rate the plume model sees.
[Normal] Design fire heat release rate for the sub-domain:
[Normal] Q = I × L_segment
[Normal]   = (10,040 kW/m) × (3.0 m)
[Normal]   = 30,120 kW
[Normal]   = 30.1 MW
[Normal] Idealizations recorded so they are not misread as physical dimensions.
[Normal] •  Flame depth and flame residence time are not resolved in this sub-domain. The flaming front is represented as an equivalent 3.0 m characteristic-diameter source patch.
[Normal] •  The wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m from Section 3 is a wind-tilted correlation length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height. Heskestad’s still-air flame-height correlation, evaluated for the same 30.1 MW heat release rate at a 3.0 m diameter source, gives roughly 11.5 m. The 5.4 m vs 11.5 m gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy between two attempts to model the same quantity.
[Normal] Plume characteristic diameter D*.  For Q = 30.1 MW and standard reference-atmosphere conditions (ρ_∞ = 1.204 kg/m³, c_p = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, T_∞ = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s²):
[Normal] D* = ( Q / ( rho_inf · c_p · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^(2/5)
[Normal]    = ( 30,100 / ( 1.204 × 1.005 × 293.15 × 3.132 ) )^(2/5)
[Normal]    = ( 27.08 )^(2/5)
[Normal] D* = 3.76 m.
[Normal] The fine-grid cell size specified for the LES mesh study is dx = 0.5 m (the finest of the three grids in the mesh study). This gives:
[Normal] D* / dx = 3.76 / 0.5 = 7.5
[Normal] which confirms the plume is adequately resolved on the fine grid. LES resolution acceptance shall be assessed per the firm QA standard applicable to reacting-plume LES.
[Normal] 6.  Wall Assembly Note
[Normal] The through-wall response of the assembly cannot be modelled as heat conduction through a single solid slab. Per the OAS-WUI-01_revC wall assembly section (Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png), the assembly is a double-wythe cavity system: two 50 mm printed-concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (overall thickness 305 mm), tied together by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties spaced 600 mm on centre vertically, embedded 25 mm into each leaf. The cavity carries no insulation. The architectural drawing (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW in its title block; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout the SOW, this memo, and all downstream analysis artifacts.
[Normal] The metallic ties are a continuous parallel thermal path between the exposed and unexposed leaves; their conductivity (~45 W/m·K) is more than an order of magnitude above the siliceous-aggregate concrete of the leaves, and they are the reason the single-point criterion governs over the average-rise criterion in the ASTM E119 test result of record.
[Normal] Per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §6, the through-wall modeling treatment for this assembly shall be selected and documented in the case setup record before meshing, accounting for the metallic ties’ thermal-bridge role identified above. Temperature-dependent solid properties (k, ρ, c_p) apply per Modeling Standard §3.5.
[Normal] 7.  Downstream Inputs
[Normal] The following quantities established above are the source-term and length-scale inputs for the downstream Phase 1 case-setup, mesh-study, and reporting artifacts:
[Normal] •  Site design envelope: ambient 35–42 °C, RH 10–25 %, 20-ft wind 5–12 m/s (Section 2).
[Normal] •  Byram fireline intensity I = 10,040 kW/m (Section 3).
[Normal] •  Wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m (Section 3).
[Normal] •  LES sub-domain fire-front segment: 3.0 m (Section 5).
[Normal] •  Design fire heat release rate: 30.1 MW (Section 5.1).
[Normal] •  Plume characteristic diameter: D* = 3.76 m (Section 5.1).
[Normal] •  Froude ratio range across the site design envelope: ~0.9–2.2 (Section 4); regime classification and solver selection per Modeling Standard §§2–3 to be documented in the case setup record (Section 4).
[Normal] •  Wall through-thickness modeling treatment: to be selected and documented per Modeling Standard §6, accounting for the metallic tie thermal-bridge path identified in Section 6.
[Normal] The 3.0 m segment, 30.1 MW source, and D* = 3.76 m established per Section 5 above are the inputs the fine grid dx = 0.5 m recorded in the Meshing and case-build log is sized against.
[Normal] The 5–12 m/s design wind envelope carries forward into the wind-inlet boundary conditions of the six-case matrix, per the solver selection made in Section 4; the puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz predicted by the f = 1.5·D^(-1/2) correlation per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §4 for this plume sets the writeInterval and end-time requirements for each transient run.
[Normal] 8.  Reviewer Sign-Off
[Normal] Prepared by:
[Normal] Gordon Selby, PE
[Normal] Owner & Principal Engineer, The CFD ME
[Normal] Arizona PE #48213
[Normal] 10/08/2025

    The firm holds current single-user licenses to the standards summarized below. This digest restates in the firm’s
    own words only the provisions the firm’s procedures rely on, with a citation back to the source clause. For any
    determination outside the summarized clauses, consult the source document. This digest may not be redistributed.
    The intent is to give firm engineers a quick, unambiguous reference to the specific clauses called out in our
    procedures (Modeling Standards, Verification Standard, Validation Procedure, Units SOP),
    without asking anyone to pull the full external standard for a routine check. Where a clause is quoted at all, it is
    paraphrased; no line of protected text is reproduced verbatim. Anyone needing the full text — for interpretation,
    for a determination outside the summarized clauses, or for any client-facing citation — must consult the licensed
    copy on the shared drive (see Section 5).

    1. ASTM E119 — Standard Test Method for Fire Tests of Building Construction and
    Materials
    Scope in firm use.
    ASTM E119 is the fire-endurance test method the firm’s assembly-rating work is anchored to. It is a laboratory
    test on a representative wall (or floor, roof, etc.) assembly exposed on one face to a controlled furnace fire that
    tracks the ASTM E119 standard building time-temperature curve.

    Standard fire exposure.
    The furnace follows the standard time-temperature curve: temperature rises rapidly in the first ten minutes and
    then continues on a defined logarithmic path (approximately 538 °C / 1000 °F at 5 minutes, 704 °C / 1300 °F at
    10 minutes, 843 °C / 1550 °F at 30 minutes, 927 °C / 1700 °F at 1 hour, and so on). The curve is a comparative
    fire exposure, not a representation of any specific real fire.

    Thermal-transmission criteria on the unexposed face.
    Two thermal-transmission criteria on the unexposed face of the assembly are monitored, both measured relative
    to the initial unexposed-face temperature at the start of the test:
           (1) Average unexposed-face temperature rise: 139 °C / 250 °F, measured as the arithmetic mean of nine
           thermocouples distributed on the unexposed face in accordance with the standard’s thermocouple placement
           pattern.
           (2) Single-point unexposed-face temperature rise: 181 °C / 325 °F, measured at any single thermocouple
           on the unexposed face.

    Governing endurance.




CFDME-FS-DIG-2025-01 | Firm-internal | Not for redistribution                                                        Page 1
 THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | External Standards Digest | rev 1 | Effective 09/01/2025
Firm-internal restatement of paid external standards; no proprietary text reproduced


    The reported endurance for the thermal-transmission criterion is the elapsed time at which the earlier of the two
    criteria is reached. If the single-point criterion is reached before the average criterion, the single-point endurance
    governs; if the average criterion is reached first, the average governs. The reported endurance is not the later of
    the two, and is not any interpolation or average of the two.

    Practical note on cavity assemblies with metal ties.
    For a double-wythe cavity assembly with continuous metal ties (galvanized truss-type ties are typical), the tie
    forms a metallic thermal bridge between the exposed and unexposed leaves. In practice this frequently drives a
    single thermocouple sitting directly over a tie to reach the 181 °C single-point criterion before the average of the
    nine thermocouples reaches 139 °C. Engineers should expect the single-point criterion to govern in assemblies of
    that construction and should not treat that outcome as anomalous.
    Cite. ASTM E119 §7 (furnace control, thermocouple placement) and §8 (unexposed-face
    temperature criteria).

    What E119 is not.
    E119 is an assembly rating test conducted under a comparative standard fire exposure. It is not a wildfire
    exposure. It is not a natural fire, a compartment fire, a facade fire, or a wildland-urban interface fire exposure. See
    Section 4.

    2. ASME V&V 20 — Standard for Verification and Validation in Computational Fluid
    Dynamics and Heat Transfer
    Scope in firm use.
    ASME V&V 20 is the framework governing how the firm reports validation of a CFD model against
    experimental data. It is the basis of the firm’s Validation QA Procedure.

    The validation comparison.
    Validation is reported as the model error

                                                                       E = S−D
    where S is the simulation prediction (the model’s value for the validation quantity of interest, produced by the
    case as run), and D is the corresponding experimental data value (produced by a certified third-party test report;
    see §S6).      E is a signed number; it is not squared, not absolute-valued, and not otherwise normalized at this
    step.

    The validation uncertainty.
    The model error E is reported together with its validation uncertainty u_val. u_val is built as the
    root-sum-square of the numerical uncertainty component, the input uncertainty component, and the
    experimental uncertainty component:

                                                   u_val = √( u_num² + u_in² + u_D² )
    where u_num is the numerical uncertainty (discretization, iterative, and round-off contributions from the
    simulation), u_in is the input uncertainty (uncertainty in boundary conditions, material properties, and other
    inputs propagated through the model), and u_D is the experimental uncertainty (uncertainty of the measured data
    value D as reported by the testing laboratory).

    Reporting.



CFDME-FS-DIG-2025-01 | Firm-internal | Not for redistribution                                                           Page 2
 THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | External Standards Digest | rev 1 | Effective 09/01/2025
Firm-internal restatement of paid external standards; no proprietary text reproduced


    Validation is reported as the pair E ± u_val, together with the comparison against the firm’s acceptance criterion.
    The reported form is never a bare “yes / no,” “pass / fail,” “validated / not validated,” or “within tolerance.” An
    engineer who cannot write down the three uncertainty components has not yet completed the validation and must
    not report a validation outcome.

    Comparison against acceptance criterion.
    The firm’s acceptance criterion is stated as a numerical bound on |E| (see §S5                for the current criterion,
    expressed as a percentage of D). The report states E, states u_val, states the criterion, and states the outcome of
    the comparison, in that order. If |E| is larger than both the criterion and u_val, the discrepancy is a resolved model
    error rather than measurement scatter, and that fact must be stated.
    Cite. ASME V&V 20 §1 (validation framework, definitions of S, D, E) and §5 (uncertainty estimation and combination).


    3. ASCE 7-22 — Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and
    Other Structures
    Scope in firm use.
    ASCE 7-22 governs the firm’s structural wind-load extraction work, including the Section 3.2 windward-wall
    pressure deliverables on projects that carry a separate structural wind case alongside a CFD scope.

    Velocity pressure.
    The velocity pressure at height z is computed as

                                                   q_z = 0.00256 · K_z · K_zt · K_e · V²
    with V in miles per hour and q_z in pounds per square foot (psf). The factors are:
         K_z — velocity pressure exposure coefficient, tabulated in ASCE 7-22 Table 26.10 as a function of height z
         above ground and Exposure Category (B, C, or D). For sites of the firm’s typical Sonoran Desert exposure
         (open terrain with scattered obstructions), Exposure C is applicable.
         K_zt — topographic factor from ASCE 7-22 §26.8. K_zt = 1.0 for essentially flat terrain (no isolated hill,
         ridge, or escarpment meeting the geometric thresholds of §26.8.1).
         K_e — ground elevation factor from ASCE 7-22 §26.9. ASCE 7-22 permits K_e = 1.0 to be used
         conservatively at all ground elevations; the tabulated value below unity may alternatively be used. Using
         K_e = 1.0 is conservative (higher q_z) at elevated sites.

    Note on K_d and where it is applied.
    In ASCE 7-22, the wind directionality factor K_d is applied in the design pressure equation, not in the velocity
    pressure equation. Do not multiply K_d into q_z. This is a change in equation form from earlier ASCE 7 revisions
    that some engineers may remember; check that any spreadsheet, template, or reference calculation reflects the
    7-22 placement.

    Windward wall design pressure.
    The design pressure on the windward wall is

                                                          p_w = q_z · G · C_p · K_d
    where:
         G — gust-effect factor from ASCE 7-22 §26.11. G = 0.85 is the default value for rigid buildings.




CFDME-FS-DIG-2025-01 | Firm-internal | Not for redistribution                                                              Page 3
 THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | External Standards Digest | rev 1 | Effective 09/01/2025
Firm-internal restatement of paid external standards; no proprietary text reproduced


         C_p — windward wall external pressure coefficient from ASCE 7-22 Figure 27.3-1. C_p = +0.8 for the
         windward wall (all L/B), by convention with the wind blowing onto the surface.
         K_d — wind directionality factor from ASCE 7-22 Table 26.6-1. K_d = 0.85 for main wind-force resisting
         systems on buildings.
    Cite. ASCE 7-22 §26.10 (velocity pressure calculation), §27.3 (external pressure coefficients for buildings, MWFRS
    Directional Procedure), and §26.6 (wind directionality factor, Table 26.6-1).


    4. ASTM E119 vs WUI — Interpretive Note
             E119 endurance is a comparative assembly rating under standard fire exposure. It is not a
             prediction of wildfire survival time. A validation against E119 data validates a model against
             E119, not against a wildfire performance claim.

    The distinction matters in practice because the same physical wall assembly may carry both an E119 endurance
    number (in minutes to the governing thermal-transmission criterion) and a separate CFD-derived wildfire
    exposure result (peak unexposed-face temperature under a Sonoran buffelgrass fire matrix, say). The two are
    answers to two different questions and may not be interchanged.
    Specifically:
         An E119 furnace fire follows the standard time-temperature curve. A wildfire, wildland-urban interface, or
         facade fire does not. Their radiative fluxes on the exposed face, their gas temperatures, their duration, and
         their variability in time are all different.
         An E119 test rates the assembly against a defined standard fire; the resulting endurance number is
         comparable across assemblies tested against the same standard. It is not portable to any specific real-world
         fire.
         A validation of a CFD model against E119 data establishes that the model reproduces the assembly’s
         behaviour under the standard E119 exposure, within the reported E ± u_val. It says nothing about the model’s
         accuracy under a wildfire boundary condition, which is a different physical regime.
    Statements of the form “the assembly survives a wildfire for X minutes” or “the model is validated for wildfire
    performance” are not supported by an E119 comparison alone and must not appear in a firm deliverable on the
    basis of an E119 validation. If the firm wishes to make a wildfire-performance claim, it must be validated against
    wildfire-relevant test data under the same framework in Section 2.

    5. License and Distribution Note
    Licenses held.
    The firm holds current single-user licenses to ASTM E119, ASME V&V 20, and ASCE 7-22. Licenses are held
    under the firm’s name (The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC) and renewed on an annual cycle by the Technical
    Director.

    Source documents.
    The licensed source PDFs are maintained on the firm’s shared drive at:
             Firm/Standards/_External/

    Every engineer with need-to-access has read access to that directory. The license terms attached to each standard
    prohibit further redistribution of the source document; do not copy the source PDF into a project folder, do not
    email it to a client or subcontractor, and do not upload it to any external service.



CFDME-FS-DIG-2025-01 | Firm-internal | Not for redistribution                                                            Page 4

Firm-internal restatement of paid external standards; no proprietary text reproduced


    Digest scope.
    This digest paraphrases only the specific provisions the firm’s procedures cite. It is not a substitute for the full
    external standard. Any determination that turns on a provision outside the clauses summarized here must be made
    against the licensed source document on the shared drive.

    Distribution of this digest.
    This digest is firm-internal. It may not be redistributed to clients, subcontractors, or any external party. Where a
    client-facing deliverable needs to state that the firm’s procedure follows one of these standards, cite the standard
    by number and clause; do not attach or quote from this digest.

THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution | rev 3 | Effective 07/01/2025

Document ID: CFDME-QA-VS-MR Revision: rev 3 Effective Date: 07/01/2025 Supersedes: rev 2 (Effective
03/15/2023) Author of Record: Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer, AZ PE #42798
Applies To: All CFD deliverables issued from The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC (The CFD ME), 4820 E River Rd,
Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718


1. Purpose & Scope
This standard establishes the firm's minimum requirements for demonstrating that a CFD result is grid-independent
(for steady Reynolds-averaged work) or adequately resolved (for large-eddy simulation), and specifies how the
underlying evidence must be presented in the Verification section of every deliverable that leaves the firm.
The standard applies to every project executed by The CFD ME staff and to every subcontracted deliverable
prepared on the firm's behalf, including work performed by Mulshi Simulation Labs and any other external contractor
operating under a CFD ME work order. Reviewing Engineer sign-off on the peer-review checklist requires explicit
confirmation that the requirements of this document have been met.
Revision 3 rewrites the LES portion of the standard. The rev 2 language treated the Roache/Richardson grid
convergence index (GCI) as the default verification instrument for every solve regardless of turbulence treatment.
Two internal audits and a client peer review in Q1 2025 established that the treatment is technically incorrect for
large-eddy simulation and produces verification evidence that will not survive third-party scrutiny. The corrected
treatment is set out in Sections 4 and 5.
Nothing in this standard modifies the firm's Validation QA Procedure & Acceptance Criterion
(Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2), the firm's Modeling Standards for Fire & Buoyant Flows
, current revision, or the Units and Conversions SOP
(Firm/Standards/CFDME_Units_SOP_rev2). Where the requirements of this standard intersect those documents, all of them
apply concurrently.

2. Definitions
Grid convergence index (GCI). A quantitative estimator of numerical uncertainty attributable to spatial discretisation
error, computed from a monotonic sequence of solutions on systematically refined grids under an assumed observed
order of accuracy. Reported as a percentage band on a selected integrated quantity of interest. The GCI is defined
for solutions that converge to a unique grid-independent limit as the mesh is refined.
Plume resolution index (D*/dx). The ratio of the characteristic plume diameter D* to the representative fire-region
cell edge length dx. D* is the buoyancy-driven length scale associated with a fire heat release rate Q_dot and is
defined as
D* = ( Q_dot / ( rho_inf · cp · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^{2/5}
where rho_inf, cp and T_inf are the ambient density, specific heat and absolute temperature respectively, and g is
gravitational acceleration. The index D*/dx is the standard measure of how many cells span the buoyancy-dominated
length scale of a fire plume.
Resolved turbulent kinetic energy (k_res). The turbulent kinetic energy carried by the explicitly resolved velocity
fluctuations in a large-eddy simulation, distinct from the sub-grid-scale contribution k_sgs modelled by the closure.
The resolved fraction is defined as k_res / (k_res + k_sgs).
RANS and steady work. In this document, "RANS and steady work" means Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes
simulations run to steady state, whether solved with a pseudo-time or true-steady solver, including internal buoyant
airflow of the type in the Copperline municipal HVAC envelope. Unsteady RANS (URANS) is treated as RANS for the
purposes of Section 4.
LES. Large-eddy simulation, including the firm's reacting-fire LES stack (fireFoam with EDC combustion and fvDOM
radiation) and any non-reacting LES of atmospheric or building flow.

3. General Requirements for Verification
Every deliverable that reports a CFD result shall contain a Verification section, plainly labelled as such, appearing in
the body of the report ahead of Validation and ahead of Results. The Verification section shall state, at minimum:
 (a) The turbulence treatment used (RANS, URANS, or LES) and, for LES, the sub-grid-scale closure.
(b) The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, and the total cell count.
(c) The verification basis chosen from Section 4 or Section 5, together with the numerical evidence supporting that
basis.
(d) A single-sentence statement identifying which acceptance criterion has been met and by what margin.
The Verification section shall not be an appendix pointer. Numerical values that support the verification claim shall
appear in the body. Supporting figures, residual histories, and mesh-slice imagery may be relegated to an appendix
and referenced.
Verification is prerequisite to Validation. A deliverable whose Verification section is absent, incomplete, or
inconsistent with this standard shall not be released for client transmission and shall not carry a Reviewing Engineer
signature.

4. Grid Convergence Index (GCI)
The Roache/Richardson grid convergence index is the firm's verification instrument for RANS and steady work only.
GCI is not valid for LES and shall not be used to verify any large-eddy result issued from this firm.
The reason is physical. Under systematic mesh refinement, an LES does not converge to a unique grid-independent
solution. As the filter width narrows, energy migrates from the modelled sub-grid-scale contribution into the explicitly
resolved field; the resolved-to-modelled turbulence split changes with the mesh. A three-grid sequence of LES
solutions therefore records a change in the physical content of the simulation between grids rather than a
discretisation-error tail collapsing toward a limit. The Richardson extrapolation on which the GCI is built assumes that
limit exists. It does not exist for LES, and therefore GCI values computed from an LES three-grid study are
numerically well-formed but physically meaningless. Non-monotonic behaviour in an LES three-grid quantity of
interest is the expected signature of the changing split, not evidence of a defective mesh study.
For RANS and steady solves, the firm applies the standard Richardson formulation. Given three systematically
refined grids with representative cell sizes h_1 < h_2 < h_3, refinement ratios r_21 = h_2 / h_1 and r_32 = h_3 / h_2
each at least 1.3, and a scalar quantity of interest phi with values phi_1, phi_2, phi_3 on the three grids, the observed
order of accuracy p is obtained from
phi_3 − phi_2 = ( r_32^p − 1 ) / ( r_21^p − 1 ) · ( phi_2 − phi_1 )
solved for p by fixed-point iteration. The fine-grid GCI on the finest pair is then
GCI_fine = F_s · | ( phi_2 − phi_1 ) / phi_1 | / ( r_21^p − 1 )
with a safety factor F_s of 1.25 when three or more grids are used. Reported GCI values shall carry the safety factor
and the observed p, and shall state the quantity of interest to which they apply. Monotonic convergence is a
precondition for reporting a GCI; oscillatory or divergent triples shall be flagged and the mesh study extended rather
than reported as a GCI band.
The requirement in this Section 4 applies without exception in the RANS envelope. Verification of a steady RANS
solve without a reported GCI (or an equivalent Roache/Richardson estimator) is not accepted.

5. LES Resolution Acceptance
For large-eddy simulations, the firm accepts either of the following as sufficient evidence that the resolution is
adequate in the fire or plume region of interest. Both are preferred; either alone is acceptable.
5.1 Plume resolution index. The plume resolution index D*/dx, computed with D* from the definition in Section 2 and
dx taken as the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region, shall fall in the band 5 to 10.
Values below 5 are insufficient to carry the buoyancy-driven length scale; values above 10 are wasteful of compute
without corresponding gain in fidelity for the classes of fires the firm simulates. Q_dot in the D* expression is the fire
heat release rate applied in the LES, in watts.
5.2 Pope resolved-TKE criterion. The resolved turbulent kinetic energy shall be at least 80% of the total turbulent
kinetic energy in the region of interest, i.e.
k_res / ( k_res + k_sgs ) >= 0.8
 This is Pope's criterion for a well-resolved LES. The ratio shall be computed on a time-average of a statistically
converged solution window (typically ten or more integral time scales, or ten or more puffing cycles for a pool-fire-like
plume). Point probes shall be located within the buoyancy-dominated flow, not on the periphery of the domain.
Either criterion, met, is acceptable. Meeting both is preferred and is the default expectation for deliverables prepared
for authorities-having-jurisdiction or life-safety end use. Neither criterion may be evaded by asserting engineering
judgement in place of the numerical evidence; where a physical constraint prevents meeting either criterion, the
constraint and its consequence shall be stated explicitly in the Verification section and the deliverable escalated to
the Reviewing Engineer before release.

6. Reporting
The Verification section of every LES deliverable shall state, directly in the body of the report:
• The fire heat release rate Q_dot used to compute D*, with units.
• The characteristic plume diameter D*, with units.
• The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, with units.
• The plume resolution index D*/dx as a dimensionless number.
• The Pope resolved-TKE fraction k_res / (k_res + k_sgs) as a percentage, together with the location of the probe(s)
   and the length of the averaging window.
These values shall appear in the running text or in a table in the Verification section itself. Placement of any of these
values in an appendix, with only a cross-reference in the Verification section, does not satisfy this standard.
GCI values shall not appear in LES deliverables. A three-grid table copied forward from a RANS template into an
LES report, whether or not it is accompanied by a GCI band, is a non-compliant Verification section under this
standard. If a three-grid mesh study has been carried out on an LES case for information (for example, to
demonstrate insensitivity of an integrated quantity), the tabulated values may be included in an appendix labelled as
a sensitivity study, but they shall not be presented as verification evidence and no GCI shall be computed from them.
The Verification section of a RANS or steady deliverable shall state the observed order of accuracy p, the fine-grid
GCI on the reported quantity of interest with its safety factor, and the refinement ratios. D*/dx and Pope's criterion do
not apply to RANS deliverables and shall not be reported there.

7. Roles
Project Engineer. Responsible for constructing the mesh study or resolution assessment appropriate to the
turbulence treatment, computing the required indices, and drafting the Verification section in accordance with
Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6.
Reviewing Engineer. Responsible for confirming, on the peer-review checklist, that the Verification section of the
deliverable meets the requirements of this standard. The confirmation is a specific line item on the checklist and shall
not be a general "verification section reviewed" tick. For an LES deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
that D*, dx, D*/dx, and the Pope resolved-TKE fraction appear in the body of the report and that no GCI value has
been carried forward from a RANS template. For a RANS or steady deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
the presence of the observed order p, the GCI band and its safety factor, and monotonic convergence of the
underlying triple.
Owner / Principal Engineer. Retains final responsibility for the stamped CFD thermal analysis and for any release of
a deliverable in which the Reviewing Engineer has flagged a Verification-section deficiency that has not been
resolved.

8. References
1. Roache, P. J. (1994). Perspective: A Method for Uniform Reporting of Grid Refinement Studies. Journal of Fluids
Engineering, 116(3), 405–413. 2. Roache, P. J. (1997). Quantification of Uncertainty in Computational Fluid
Dynamics. Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics, 29, 123–160. 3. Richardson, L. F. (1911). The Approximate
Arithmetical Solution by Finite Differences of Physical Problems. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A,
210, 307–357. 4. Celik, I. B., Ghia, U., Roache, P. J., Freitas, C. J., Coleman, H., & Raad, P. E. (2008). Procedure for
Estimation and Reporting of Uncertainty Due to Discretization in CFD Applications. Journal of Fluids Engineering,
130(7), 078001. 5. Pope, S. B. (2000). Turbulent Flows. Cambridge University Press. (Chapter 13, resolved-TKE
 criterion for LES adequacy.) 6. Pope, S. B. (2004). Ten questions concerning the large-eddy simulation of turbulent
flows. New Journal of Physics, 6, 35. 7. McDermott, R., McGrattan, K., and Hostikka, S. (2008). Fire Dynamics
Simulator (FDS) Technical Reference Guide — Verification. NIST Special Publication 1018 (definition and use of the
plume resolution index D*/dx). 8. ASME V&V 20-2009 (R2016). Standard for Verification and Validation in
Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer. 9. AIAA G-077-1998 (R2002). Guide for the Verification and
Validation of Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulations. 10. The CFD ME. CFD Modeling Standards — Fire &
Buoyant Flows, current revision. 11. The CFD ME. Validation QA
Procedure & Acceptance Criterion rev 2 (Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2). 12. The CFD ME. External
Standards Digest, current revision.

Issued and signed:
Marguerite Falk, PE Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC AZ PE #42798

THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | AZ PE #48213 | Project: CFDME-2024-018 Dry Wash Aerospace | Validation
Memo | rev 1 | Issued 11/15/2024

Client: Dry Wash Aerospace Research, 15810 N Cave Creek Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85032 Prepared by: Gordon Selby,
PE (AZ PE #48213), The CFD ME Reviewed by: Marguerite Falk, PE (AZ PE #42798), Technical Director Subject:
Validation of the Dry Wash high-altitude external aerodynamics case against wind-tunnel data.


1. Purpose
This memo documents validation of the Dry Wash high-altitude external aerodynamics case (CFDME-2024-018)
against the wind-tunnel measurements of record for the airframe geometry and freestream conditions covered by the
Dry Wash SOW. It records the comparison of computed and measured surface pressure coefficients across the
operating envelope, states the envelope in which the case is validated, and states the conditions under which that
status does not transfer.
The output of this memo is a validated status attached to a specific case within a specifically bounded envelope. It is
not a certification of the geometry, the solver, or any directory containing the case files. Reuse outside the stated
envelope requires re-validation per firm modeling standards.

2. Case Description
The validated case is archived at:
CFDME-2024-018/Case/DWA_highaltitude_case_setup.txt
Salient features of the case, restated from the archive:
• Solver: rhoSimpleFoam — steady-state, pressure-based, compressible.
• Chemistry / reactions: none. The case is compressible non-reacting. No reactive scalar transport is compiled
   into the solve, and there is no combustion model.
• Radiation: off. The constant/ directory carries no radiationProperties dictionary and no radiative source
   terms in fvOptions. There is no radiation model present or exercised.
• Turbulence: RAS, k-omega SST, wall-function resolved (kqRWallFunction / omegaWallFunction /
   nutkWallFunction on all no-slip surfaces). Wall functions are used throughout; no low-Re wall resolution is
   required within the validated envelope.
• Freestream: high-altitude flight conditions — reference pressure 26,500 Pa, reference temperature 223 K,
   freestream density 0.4 kg/m3 at altitude, Mach 0.25, fully turbulent Reynolds regime.
• Boundary conditions: airframe treated as adiabatic no-slip wall; farfield freestream on the outer boundary. No
   conjugate heat-transfer regions, no cavity or multi-region entries.
• Time stepping: steady-state (ddtSchemes default steadyState, adjustTimeStep no, endTime in
   iterations).
The case as archived matches, without modification, the case that produced the computed pressure coefficients
reported in Section 4.

3. Validation Data
The reference data set is the wind-tunnel surface-pressure coefficient measurement campaign run by Dry Wash
Aerospace Research in 2022-Q4 on the airframe geometry of record. The dataset consists of surface pressure
coefficient (Cp) taps distributed across the body at stations covering the operating envelope; both freestream Mach
and angle-of-attack were swept in the tunnel to match the CFD sweep.
The reference dataset carries pressure coefficients only. It does not contain:
• surface or gas temperature measurements,
• heat flux measurements,
• any reacting-flow scalar (species mass fractions, heat-release rate, radiant intensity),
 • any buoyancy-driven quantity.
The dataset is therefore an aerodynamic-loads reference. It bounds what a comparison to this data can establish:
agreement in surface pressure distribution under high-altitude, low-density, non-reacting compressible flow over the
fixed body. It does not bound thermal, reacting, or buoyancy-dominated performance and cannot be used to argue for
validation in those regimes.

4. Comparison — Cp_computed vs Cp_measured
Computed and measured pressure coefficients were compared at every instrumented station across the operating
envelope. Agreement is within 4% at all stations. The station-by-station delta_Cp summary is reproduced below.
Table 4.1 — delta_Cp = Cp_computed − Cp_measured, absolute percent of measured Cp, by station and operating
point.

5. Validated Envelope
This validation applies only within the envelope: high-altitude, low-density (0.4 kg/m3 against 1.2 kg/m3 at sea level),
non-reacting compressible aerodynamics over a fixed body. No combustion or radiation models were present or
exercised. Extension to reacting flows, buoyancy-dominated flows, or ground-level (sea-level density) applications
requires re-validation. Validated status attaches to a case within an envelope, not to a directory or a geometry.
The envelope statement is normative for the disposition of this case. Its boundaries are:
• Aerodynamic regime: high-altitude external aerodynamics; freestream density 0.4 kg/m3, not 1.2 kg/m3
   sea-level air.
• Validated Mach range: 0.20–0.30 (the range covered by the DWA-WT-2022-Q4 wind-tunnel dataset and Table
   4.1 of this memo). The SOW Attachment A Cruise Envelope of Mach 0.60–0.85 is NOT covered by the validation
   data set; extension of validated status to the full contractual cruise Mach range requires additional wind-tunnel or
   flight-test data.
• Physics compiled and exercised: compressible steady RANS; no combustion; no radiation; no conjugate heat
   transfer; no buoyancy source.
• Body condition: fixed rigid body, adiabatic wall.
• Reference data: surface pressure coefficients from the 2022-Q4 wind-tunnel campaign; no thermal, no reacting
   quantity.
 Any application outside all four boundaries above is outside the validated envelope. In particular, the case is not
validated for ground-level applications, for reacting flow of any kind, for buoyancy-dominated flow, or for anything
requiring a thermal or reacting reference beyond the pressure-coefficient dataset used here.

The validated envelope stated in Section 5 does not transfer across regimes; any reuse of this case outside the
Section 5 envelope requires re-validation per firm modeling standards.
Additional limitations bearing on interpretation of this memo:
1. Contractual cruise Mach range not covered. The DWA-WT-2022-Q4 wind-tunnel dataset used as reference
here sits in the Mach 0.20–0.30 band; the SOW Attachment A Cruise Envelope of Mach 0.60–0.85 lies outside the
validated range. Extension of the validated designation to the full contractual cruise Mach range requires additional
wind-tunnel or flight-test data. 2. The comparison is against surface pressure coefficient only. Any downstream use
that depends on quantities not measured in the reference campaign (e.g., surface heat flux, species distribution,
radiant flux) is unsupported by this validation. 3. Wall functions were used. Cases whose acceptance depends on
resolved near-wall thermal or laminar-transition behavior are outside scope and require an independent validation
basis. 4. Steady RANS was used. Cases whose physics are inherently transient (e.g., separated wake unsteadiness
at high alpha, puffing plumes) are outside scope. 5. The freestream density anchoring the envelope is 0.4 kg/m3. A
change to 1.2 kg/m3 sea-level air is a change of physical regime, not a change of operating point, and voids the
validated status. 6. Validated status attaches to this case in this envelope. It does not attach to the directory
CFDME-2024-018/Case/, to the airframe geometry file, to the solver rhoSimpleFoam, or to any set of dictionaries

STATEMENT OF WORK
Consulting Engineering Services — Fixed Fee

SOW No.:                                                    CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01
Project No.:                                                CFDME-2025-041
Project Name:                                               Ocotillo WUI Wildfire, Phase 1
Date:                                                       10/08/2025

This Statement of Work ("SOW") is entered into as of 10/08/2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between The CFD
Mechanical Engineer, LLC, an Arizona limited liability company doing business as The CFD ME, with offices at 4820
E River Rd, Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718 ("Consultant"), and Ocotillo Additive Structures, with offices at 3175 S Palo
Verde Rd, Tucson, AZ 85713 ("Client"). The parties agree as follows.


1. Purpose and Background
Client designs and constructs single-family residential structures using proprietary additive-manufactured (3D-printed)
portland-cement concrete wall assemblies and intends to market those structures for siting within the wildland-urban
interface ("WUI") of the Sonoran Desert west of Tucson, Arizona. Client's marketing programme advances the
positioning that Client's printed-concrete envelope is more fire-resistant, under credible wildfire exposure, than
conventional wood-frame construction of comparable footprint.
Consultant is engaged to provide the computational-fluid-dynamics ("CFD") backing for that positioning as it applies
to a Sonoran Desert buffelgrass wildfire event in the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson. The engagement
covers Phase 1 only: the mixed-convection wildfire plume analyses enumerated in Section 3.1 and the structural
wind-pressure extraction enumerated in Section 3.2, together with the deliverables in Section 4.
Client acknowledges that fire-resistance ratings on the printed wall assembly (including the current 1-hour rating
already issued by others) are outside the scope of this SOW and are certified separately by a third-party
fire-protection engineer under a separate engagement. This SOW procures analysis only.


2. Definitions
For purposes of this SOW, the following terms have the meanings given below.
"Assembly" — the double-wythe printed-concrete wall system, geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC as
transmitted by Client to Consultant on the Effective Date.
"Buffelgrass Fuel Model" — the Sonoran-desert buffelgrass ground-fuel model adopted for the wildfire source term
in the Section 3.1 matrix, as documented in Consultant's Phase 1 scoping memo of even date.
"LES" — large-eddy simulation, meaning transient turbulence-resolving CFD run with wall time-step control per
Consultant's internal modelling standard for reacting buoyant flows.
"Site" — the Avra Valley Sonoran Desert WUI parcel west of Tucson identified in Client's Phase 0 site file.
"Wildfire Matrix" — the six-case matrix of atmospheric conditions and wind directions defined in Section 3.1.
"Structural Wind Case" — the single ASCE 7-22 wind-pressure load case defined in Section 3.2.
"Change Order" — a written amendment to this SOW, executed by both parties, before performance, that modifies
scope, schedule, or fee.


3. Scope of Work
Consultant shall perform the services set out in Sections 3.1 and 3.2 below. Section 3.1 and Section 3.2 are separate
load cases with separate governing bases; results from one shall not be substituted for or compared against results
from the other.

3.1 Wildfire Analysis Matrix
 Consultant shall execute a matrix of six (6) transient mixed-convection wildfire simulations against the Assembly at
the Site, using Consultant's fireFoam-based LES stack with EDC combustion, fvDOM radiation, and
atmospheric-boundary-layer inlet, per Consultant's internal Modeling Standard for Fire & Buoyant Flows. The matrix
crosses two (2) wind directions with three (3) mean wind speeds at 20 ft reference height, as follows.

Case                  Wind Direction    Wind Speed (20      Ambient             Relative Humidity Fuel
                                        ft)
3.1-A                 240 deg           5 m/s               35–42 °C            10–25 %             Buffelgrass
3.1-B                 240 deg           8 m/s               35–42 °C            10–25 %             Buffelgrass
3.1-C                 240 deg           12 m/s              35–42 °C            10–25 %             Buffelgrass
3.1-D                 270 deg           5 m/s               35–42 °C            10–25 %             Buffelgrass
3.1-E                 270 deg           8 m/s               35–42 °C            10–25 %             Buffelgrass
3.1-F                 270 deg           12 m/s              35–42 °C            10–25 %             Buffelgrass

The matrix is defined by the six combinations of the two (2) wind directions — 240 deg and 270 deg — with the three
(3) mean wind speeds at 20 ft reference height — 5, 8, and 12 m/s. Site meteorological ranges above are drawn from
the ten-year Pima County ALERT record for the Avra Valley station and are furnished as environmental context for
the six enumerated cases; they do not constitute additional cases beyond the six listed.
Each case shall be run to a physical simulated time covering not fewer than twenty (20) puffing cycles of the plume as
characterized in Consultant's scoping memo. Output for each case shall include: incident heat flux and gas
temperatures at the exposed face of the Assembly; conjugate through-wall temperature history at the tie and
mid-panel locations; and the plume flow field in the vicinity of the structure.

3.2 Structural Wind-Pressure Extraction (ASCE 7-22)
Separately from and independent of the Section 3.1 matrix, Consultant shall extract the design wind pressures on the
windward face of the Assembly at the Site per ASCE 7-22, Chapter 26 (velocity pressure) and Chapter 27 (main wind
force resisting system, directional procedure), for the following parameters:
• Site: Tucson, Arizona
• Basic wind speed, V: 96 mph
• Exposure Category: C
• Risk Category: II
• Enclosure classification: enclosed
• Mean roof height: 6.4 m
• Topographic factor K_zt: 1.0
• Ground elevation factor K_e: 1.0
• Directionality factor K_d: 0.85
• Gust-effect factor G: 0.85
• Windward wall pressure coefficient C_p: 0.8
Section 3.2 is a distinct load case, not part of the Section 3.1 matrix. The Section 3.2 result is a code-basis
structural design pressure derived from the ASCE 7-22 procedure with the parameters listed above. It shall not be
substituted for, added to, or interchanged with the wildfire-plume flow-field pressures produced under Section 3.1,
which arise from a different physical regime at different reference wind speeds. Section 3.1 results are transient
plume-flow quantities; the Section 3.2 result is a code-basis design pressure. Consultant shall report each in its own
governing units alongside its governing boundary condition.


4. Deliverables
 Consultant shall issue the following deliverables to Client, each in Consultant's standard filename convention
(revision letters, never dates or "final"):
1. Interim first-principles hand-calc memo. A short technical memorandum documenting the
Rothermel-to-Byram-to-solid-flame radiation chain used to size the LES source term, issued for Client information
ahead of the LES setup. 2. Mixed-convection LES setup memo. A technical memorandum documenting the
fireFoam case setup for the Section 3.1 matrix, including solver stack, combustion and radiation models, atmospheric
boundary layer inlet, plume characteristic diameter, mesh study, and the LES resolution basis (D*/dx and Pope
resolved-TKE indicators). Issued reviewed. 3. Structural wind-load basis memo. A technical memorandum
documenting the Section 3.2 ASCE 7-22 extraction, including the parameter set of Section 3.2 and the resulting
windward-wall design pressure in both US customary and SI units. Issued reviewed. 4. Phase 1 report. A single
consolidated report presenting the Section 3.1 wildfire-matrix results and the Section 3.2 structural wind-pressure
result, with Verification and Validation sections stated per Consultant's internal QA standards, and bearing
peer-review sign-off by Consultant's Reviewing Engineer prior to release to Client.
Consultant's professional seal, where applied, extends only to the CFD thermal analysis and carries Consultant's
stamp boundary: fire-resistance rating certified separately by others.


5. Sprint Cadence
The work shall proceed on weekly sprints beginning Monday 10/13/2025. The interim milestones and delivery targets
are:

Sprint                                  Due                                     Milestone
Sprint 1                                10/13/2025                              First-principles hand-calc interim
                                                                                memo (Rothermel → Byram →
                                                                                solid-flame radiation)
Sprint 2                                10/20/2025                              Mixed-convection LES setup memo
                                                                                and D*/dx resolution check
—                                       10/27/2025                              Confirmatory ASTM E119 test
                                                                                window at Red Butte Fire & Materials
                                                                                Testing (Client-commissioned;
                                                                                Consultant participates for
                                                                                instrumentation and companion-sim
                                                                                alignment only)
Delivery                                11/07/2025                              Validation review (E ± u_val),
                                                                                peer-review sign-off, and Phase 1
                                                                                report delivered to Client

Schedule assumes Client turnaround of not more than one (1) business day on information requests bearing on the
critical path. Slippage in Client turnaround shifts the Phase 1 delivery date on a day-for-day basis.


6. Fees and Payment
The fee for Phase 1 is a fixed fee of $84,500, inclusive of labor, internal cluster compute time on Consultant's
"borrego" cluster, cloud-burst compute if invoked, and ordinary expenses. The fixed fee is not adjusted for effort
actually expended within the scope defined in Sections 3.1 and 3.2. Consultant shall invoice as follows:

Invoice                                 Trigger                                 Amount
1                                       At signature (Effective Date)           $33,800 (40%)
2                                       Delivery of mixed-convection LES        $25,350 (30%)
                                        setup memo
3                                       Delivery of Phase 1 report              $25,350 (30%)
 Invoices are payable net thirty (30) days from date of issue. Amounts remaining unpaid past due bear interest at the
lower of 1.0 % per month or the maximum rate permitted by Arizona law.


7. Standards Referenced
The following external standards govern the technical work under this SOW to the extent stated in the corresponding
deliverable:
• ASCE 7-22 — Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures. Governs
   Section 3.2 velocity-pressure and wall-pressure-coefficient procedure.
• ASME V&V 20 — Standard for Verification and Validation in Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer.
   Governs the Phase 1 report Validation section and Consultant's E = S − D formulation with combined u_val.
• ASTM E119 — Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests of Building Construction and Materials. Governs the
   assembly fire-endurance test procured by Client from Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing and referenced as the
   comparative-rating basis. ASTM E119 endurance is a comparative assembly rating, not a wildfire survival
   prediction; the two are not interchangeable and shall not be treated as such in any deliverable under this SOW.
Consultant holds single-user licenses to the standards above.


8. Change Orders
Any work outside the Section 3.1 Wildfire Matrix and the Section 3.2 Structural Wind Case requires a written change
order, executed by both parties before the additional work is performed. Without limitation, the following constitute
out-of-scope work and require a change order before performance: additional wind directions beyond 240 deg and
270 deg; additional wind speeds beyond 5, 8, and 12 m/s; different fuel models; different assemblies or geometry
revisions superseding the geometry of record; additional structural load cases beyond the Section 3.2 case; and any
determination of ratings, listings, or certifications.
A change order shall state the incremental scope, the incremental fee, and any adjustment to the Section 5 schedule.
Consultant shall not begin change-order work before the change order is signed by both parties.


9. Confidentiality
Each party shall treat as confidential the non-public technical, commercial, and personnel information of the other
received in connection with this SOW, shall use such information only for purposes of performance hereunder, and
shall protect it with not less than the degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of like character.
Confidentiality obligations survive termination for a period of five (5) years. Excluded from confidentiality: information
that (a) is or becomes public other than through breach by the receiving party; (b) was known to the receiving party
without obligation of confidence before receipt; (c) is received from a third party without obligation of confidence; or
(d) is required to be disclosed by law or regulatory authority, in which case the receiving party shall give prompt notice
sufficient to permit the disclosing party to seek a protective order.


10. Limitations of Liability
Consultant's services under this SOW are analysis only. Consultant does not certify fire-resistance ratings on the
Assembly; the certified fire-resistance rating on the Assembly is issued and stamped separately by others under a
separate engagement, and no seal or opinion of Consultant shall be construed as extending to that rating.
Consultant's services shall be performed consistent with the degree of skill and care ordinarily exercised by members
of the same profession practicing under similar conditions in the same locality in Arizona; no other warranty, express
or implied, is made.
Consultant's aggregate liability under this SOW, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, shall not exceed the fees
actually paid to Consultant by Client under this SOW. Neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential,
incidental, indirect, punitive, or special damages, or for lost profits, revenue, or business opportunity, arising out of or
relating to this SOW, regardless of the theory of liability and regardless of whether the party has been advised of the
possibility of such damages. Nothing herein limits liability for a party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.
 Client acknowledges that field wildfire outcomes are subject to numerous factors outside the modelled envelope of
Section 3.1 (including but not limited to ignition-source location, fuel-load spatial variability, structural condition at the
time of event, ember-cast, fire-crew intervention, and pre-fire fuel treatment), and that no CFD result under this SOW
constitutes a prediction of survival of any particular structure in any particular fire event.


11. Signatures

To: Project file, CFDME-2025-041 (Ocotillo WUI, Phase 1) From: Gordon Selby, PE — The CFD Mechanical
Engineer, LLC Subject: Structural Wind-Load Basis Memo (SOW §3.2) Prepared: 10/09/2025. Basis of the
structural wind-load extraction called out in SOW §3.2 — ASCE 7-22 procedure, site parameters, velocity pressure,
and wall design pressures for the Ocotillo Additive Structures wall assembly at the Avra Valley WUI site.


1. Purpose and scope
This memo restates, in the firm's own words, the ASCE 7-22 procedure applied to the structural wind-load extraction
required under Section 3.2 of the signed Statement of Work (executed 2025-10-08). The output of that
extraction is the set of design wind pressures on the Ocotillo double-wythe printed-concrete wall assembly at the Avra
Valley WUI site, expressed both in US customary units (psf) and in SI (Pa) per the firm's Units and Conversions SOP.
The scope of this memo is limited to the structural load case defined in Section 3.2 of the SOW. It is not the wildfire
exposure matrix defined in Section 3.1 of the same SOW; the two load cases are physically and procedurally distinct,
and — as recorded in §5 below — a pressure or velocity reported from one may not be used to check the boundary
conditions of the other. External standards referred to in this memo (ASCE 7-22 §26 and §27) are summarized under
the firm's single-user license per the External Standards Digest (rev 1); no proprietary text is reproduced.

2. Site parameters
The site is the Ocotillo Additive Structures Sonoran-Desert WUI parcel west of Tucson (Avra Valley), Pima County,
Arizona. Site parameters used to enter the ASCE 7-22 wind procedure are as follows.

Parameter                                Value                                    Source

Basic wind speed, V                      96 mph (3-s gust)                        ASCE 7-22 Fig. 26.5-1B, Risk Cat II,
                                                                                  Tucson

The occupancy is ordinary and the structure does not fall within the definitions of Risk Category III or IV, so Risk
Category II governs. The Avra Valley parcel is open desert with scattered creosote, mesquite, and buffelgrass ground
cover extending well beyond 20·h upwind in all directions relevant to the design wind rose; there is no built or forested
surface roughness of the kind that would qualify the site as Exposure B, and the site is not on open water, so
Exposure C is the correct assignment per ASCE 7-22 §26.7.3.

3. Velocity pressure
The velocity pressure at mean roof height h = 6.4 m is computed per ASCE 7-22 Eq. 26.10-1:
q_z = 0.00256 · K_z · K_zt · K_e · V² = 0.00256 · 0.91 · 1.0 · 1.0 · (96)² = 21.5 psf. Per ASCE 7-22 the wind
directionality factor K_d is applied in the design pressure equation (not the velocity pressure equation).
Arithmetic check: 0.00256 × 0.91 = 0.0023296; × 96² = × 9216 = 21.469 psf, rounded to q_z = 21.5 psf. In SI, 21.5
psf × 47.88 Pa/psf ≈ 1029 Pa.

4. Windward wall design pressure
For the main wind-force resisting system on an enclosed rigid building, the wall pressure on the windward face is
taken as
p_w = q_z · G · C_p · K_d = 21.5 · 0.85 · 0.8 · 0.85 = 12.41 psf, reported as 12.4 psf, which is 594 Pa at 1 psf =
47.88 Pa.
Where:
• G = 0.85 — gust-effect factor for a rigid building (natural frequency > 1 Hz), ASCE 7-22 §26.11.1;
• C_p = 0.8 — external pressure coefficient for the windward wall of an enclosed building, ASCE 7-22 Figure
   27.3-1;
• K_d = 0.85 — as tabulated in §2.1a above.
Arithmetic check: 21.5 × 0.85 = 18.275; × 0.8 = 14.62; × 0.85 = 12.427 psf → rounded to 12.4 psf. Conversion: 12.4 ×
47.88 = 593.7 Pa → rounded to 594 Pa.

Signs follow the ASCE convention: positive pressure acts toward the surface, negative pressure (suction) acts away
from the surface. The controlling load combinations for the wall panel and its ties are the strength-design
combinations of ASCE 7-22 Chapter 2 with the wind load W taken from this basis; those combinations are outside the
scope of this memo and will be applied in the structural check itself.
 Authority. The design pressures in the table above are the governing values for the Section 3.2 structural wind-load
extraction. Any surface pressure produced by the CFD probe extraction for this load case that does not agree in
magnitude with the corresponding row above shall be reconciled against this memo before appearing in any
client-facing deliverable. Peer-review item 9 tracks that reconciliation to close.

5. Section 3.1 versus Section 3.2 — the two load cases must not be conflated
This load case (SOW §3.2) is separate from the Section 3.1 wildfire exposure matrix. Section 3.1 runs at 5–12 m/s
(11.2–26.8 mph), where the velocity pressure is approximately
q_z ~ 0.00256 · 0.91 · (11.2 to 26.8)² ~ 0.29 to 1.68 psf ~ 14-80 Pa,
and windward wall loading is on the order of 60 Pa. A pressure reported from the §3.1 case cannot be checked
against the boundary conditions of the §3.2 case, and vice versa. The two must not be conflated.
Practically, this has two consequences for anyone reading downstream case files, probe rollups, or draft-report
tables:
1. A pressure reported at the wall surface of a Section 3.1 wildfire-matrix case that is on the order of tens of pascals is
consistent with the boundary conditions of that case and is not to be compared to the 594 Pa windward pressure of
this Section 3.2 case. 2. Section 3.2 results must be cross-checked against the boundary conditions documented in
this memo per the procedure in the firm's Units and Conversions SOP (§4) before rollup to any deliverable.
Both cases share the same wall assembly geometry (OAS-WUI-01_revC) and the same nominal site air density (1.2
kg/m³), but the physical regimes, boundary conditions, and reported quantities are otherwise disjoint.

This note documents the validation of the Copperline building-airflow case archived at /Projects/CFDME-2025-0
33_Copperline_HVAC/Case/system_archive/CPL_buoyant_case_setup.txt. Validation is performed

subsequent reuse — the physical regime under which the archived case has been shown to reproduce the field data,
and the envelope within which the "validated" designation applies.
Nothing in this note is a validation of the archived case outside that envelope. Reuse outside the envelope described
in Section 5 requires fresh validation.

2. Case Description
The archived case is a steady, incompressible-approximation OpenFOAM setup representing interior building airflow
at municipal-HVAC supply conditions. The relevant physics elements are:
• Solver. buoyantSimpleFoam — steady, single-fluid, single-phase air, buoyancy handled via the Boussinesq
   approximation (density held at ρ■; the buoyant body force is ρ■·β·(T − T_ref)·g). Pressure–velocity coupling by
   SIMPLE with under-relaxation.
• Turbulence. RAS with the standard k–ε closure. Standard wall functions on all no-slip walls (kqRWallFunction,
   epsilonWallFunction, nutkWallFunction).
• Supply inlet. fixedValue boundary at the diffuser face, uniform velocity magnitude 0.4 m/s along the diffuser
   normal, supply temperature 293.15 K (20 °C).
• Sources. fvModels and fvOptions carry no active entries. No heat-release, chemistry, mass, or momentum
   sources are applied. No chemistryProperties dictionary is loaded. No combustion model is present.
• Radiative transport. No radiationProperties dictionary is loaded. No fvDOM, P1, or viewFactor entries
   are present anywhere in the case. No radiation model is present. Interior air at the design supply state is
   optically thin over the room scale.
• External envelope walls. Adiabatic. zeroGradient on temperature, fixedFluxPressure on p_rgh, noSlip
   on velocity. No through-wall conductive or radiative flux is modelled.
• Schemes. steadyState ddt; first-order upwind on the advected scalars (T, k, ε) and on the momentum
   equation; corrected Laplacian; linear interpolation.
• Time control. endTime = 2000 SIMPLE iterations; adjustTimeStep inactive; writeControl timeStep.
   The solve is steady; no physical time integration is performed.
The case is a small-perturbation buoyant HVAC solve. It is not a reacting-flow case, not a radiation-participating case,
and not a transient case.

Two independent instrument streams were recorded in the occupied space of the Copperline municipal building over
a two-week deployment (2025-07-28 through 2025-08-10), with the data used subsequently to support

    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if not part:
            continue
        r = p.add_run(part)
        r.bold = base_bold or (i % 2 == 1)
        r.italic = italic
        if size:
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color is not None:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
    return p


def para(text, size=None, bold=False, italic=False, align=None, space_after=None,
         space_before=None, color=None, keep_next=False, indent=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text, size=size, color=color, italic=italic, base_bold=bold)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if space_after is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if space_before is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
    if keep_next:
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    if indent is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    return p


def heading(text, level=1):

    r.font.color.rgb = DARK
    r.font.size = Pt(12 if level == 1 else 10.5)

        b.set(qn("w:space"), "1")
        b.set(qn("w:color"), "8496B0")
        bdr.append(b)
        pPr.append(bdr)
    return p


def bullets(items, style="List Bullet", size=None):
    for it in items:
        p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
        add_runs(p, it, size=size)


def table(rows, widths, header=True, size=TABLE_PT, header_fill="D9E2F3",
          bold_first_col=False, align_center_cols=(), fills=None):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=len(rows), cols=len(rows[0]))

    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    cell_margins(t)

            c.paragraphs[0].text = ""

                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
                p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
                is_head = header and i == 0
                add_runs(p, line, size=size,

                if j in align_center_cols and not (header and i == 0 and False):
                    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            if header and i == 0:

            if fills and (i, j) in fills:

    # repeat header row
    if header:

        th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader")
        th.set(qn("w:val"), "true")

    # set grid widths too (LibreOffice honours tblGrid)
    grid = t._tbl.tblGrid
    for j, gc in enumerate(grid.findall(qn("w:gridCol"))):

    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)

r2 = fp.add_run(); r2.font.size = Pt(8); r2.font.color.rgb = GREY; add_field(r2, "PAGE")
